records.explanation: Variant B converts at 44.4% against 39.7% for A, a 4.8-point gain with a z-statistic of 7.43, well past the 1.96 cutoff for 95% significance.
records.sql:
WITH exp AS (
  SELECT experiment_id
  FROM reporting.experiments
  WHERE experiment_name = 'Product page: new screenshots'
),
agg AS (
  SELECT d.variant,
         SUM(d.taps)::numeric AS n,
         SUM(d.installs)::numeric AS x
  FROM reporting.experiment_daily d
  JOIN exp e ON e.experiment_id = d.experiment_id
  WHERE d.variant IN ('A', 'B')
  GROUP BY d.variant
),
s AS (
  SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN variant = 'A' THEN n END) AS nA,
         MAX(CASE WHEN variant = 'A' THEN x END) AS xA,
         MAX(CASE WHEN variant = 'B' THEN n END) AS nB,
         MAX(CASE WHEN variant = 'B' THEN x END) AS xB
  FROM agg
),
r AS (
  SELECT nA, xA, nB, xB,
         xA / NULLIF(nA, 0) AS pA,
         xB / NULLIF(nB, 0) AS pB,
         (xA + xB) / NULLIF(nA + nB, 0) AS p
  FROM s
),
z AS (
  SELECT *,
         (pB - pA) / NULLIF(sqrt(p * (1 - p) * (1 / NULLIF(nA, 0) + 1 / NULLIF(nB, 0))), 0) AS z_stat
  FROM r
)
SELECT pA AS conv_rate_A,
       pB AS conv_rate_B,
       pB - pA AS abs_diff,
       z_stat,
       ABS(z_stat) > 1.96 AS significant_at_95
FROM z;

records.explanation: Variant B's install rate (42.4%) is 0.2 points below A's (42.6%), with a z-score of -0.31, well short of the 1.96 threshold for 95% significance.
records.sql:
WITH e AS (
  SELECT experiment_id
  FROM reporting.experiments
  WHERE experiment_name = 'Product page: shorter subtitle'
),
agg AS (
  SELECT d.variant,
         SUM(d.taps)::numeric AS n,
         SUM(d.installs)::numeric AS x
  FROM reporting.experiment_daily d
  JOIN e ON e.experiment_id = d.experiment_id
  WHERE d.variant IN ('A', 'B')
  GROUP BY d.variant
),
ab AS (
  SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN variant = 'A' THEN n END) AS nA,
         MAX(CASE WHEN variant = 'A' THEN x END) AS xA,
         MAX(CASE WHEN variant = 'B' THEN n END) AS nB,
         MAX(CASE WHEN variant = 'B' THEN x END) AS xB
  FROM agg
),
stats AS (
  SELECT nA, xA, nB, xB,
         xA / nA AS pA,
         xB / nB AS pB,
         (xA + xB) / (nA + nB) AS pPooled
  FROM ab
)
SELECT pA,
       pB,
       pB - pA AS diff_b_minus_a,
       (pB - pA) / SQRT(pPooled * (1 - pPooled) * (1 / nA + 1 / nB)) AS z_score,
       CASE
         WHEN ABS((pB - pA) / SQRT(pPooled * (1 - pPooled) * (1 / nA + 1 / nB))) > 1.96
         THEN 'yes'
         ELSE 'no'
       END AS significant_95_two_sided
FROM stats;

records.explanation: "ledgerly budget" had the lowest cost per install among keywords with at least 1,000 installs, at about $0.54 (1,657 installs, about $896 spend), but the query left-joins FX rates, so any non-USD day with no matching rate drops its spend silently, which could make this figure too low, and I did not check FX coverage.
records.sql:
WITH kd AS (
  SELECT k.keyword_id, k.keyword, c.currency, d.day, d.installs, d.spend
  FROM reporting.keyword_daily d
  JOIN reporting.keywords k ON k.keyword_id = d.keyword_id
  JOIN reporting.ad_groups ag ON ag.ad_group_id = k.ad_group_id
  JOIN reporting.campaigns c ON c.campaign_id = ag.campaign_id
),
usd AS (
  SELECT kd.keyword_id, kd.keyword, kd.installs,
         kd.spend / CASE WHEN kd.currency = 'USD' THEN 1 ELSE fx.units_per_usd END AS spend_usd
  FROM kd
  LEFT JOIN reporting.fx_rates fx ON fx.day = kd.day AND fx.currency = kd.currency
),
agg AS (
  SELECT keyword_id, keyword, SUM(installs) AS installs, SUM(spend_usd) AS spend_usd
  FROM usd
  GROUP BY keyword_id, keyword
)
SELECT keyword_id, keyword, installs, spend_usd, spend_usd / installs AS cpi_usd
FROM agg
WHERE installs >= 1000
ORDER BY cpi_usd ASC
LIMIT 1;

records.explanation: The warehouse suppresses the install count for men 55+ on Sprout - JP - Search on 2026-10-01 because it is under 50, so the exact number is not available (it is not zero).
records.sql:
SELECT a.gender, a.age_band, SUM(a.installs) AS installs
FROM reporting.audience_daily AS a
JOIN reporting.campaigns AS c ON c.campaign_id = a.campaign_id
WHERE c.campaign_name = 'Sprout - JP - Search'
  AND a.day = DATE '2026-10-01'
GROUP BY a.gender, a.age_band
ORDER BY a.gender, a.age_band;

records.explanation: The warehouse has no user-level data: reporting.keyword_daily only holds daily keyword totals (impressions, taps, installs, spend), and no table has a user or person identifier, so the users who tapped 'ynab' on 2026-10-25 cannot be listed.

The warehouse returned all 10 age-and-gender groups for Trailhead - GB - Search on 2026-10-26, but each has fewer than 50 installs, so the install counts are suppressed and no numbers can be given (they are not zero).

records.explanation: None of the listed reporting tables has a revenue or in-app purchase column: campaigns, audience_daily, keyword_daily and experiment_daily carry only impressions, taps, installs and spend, so in-app purchase revenue cannot be measured from this warehouse.

The warehouse only holds this account's own keyword bids (reporting.keywords.bid) and has no competitor auction or bid data, so competitor bids for 'alltrails' cannot be found; the account's own bid on that keyword could be looked up if that helps.
